title: DOH Executive Communications & Vector Control GPS: The Ward 8 Stormwater Crisis

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

TO: doh.foia@dc.gov, carl.filler@dc.gov
CC: ayanna.bennett@dc.gov, chenderson@dccouncil.gov, rwhite@dccouncil.gov, swilson@dccouncil.gov, ldonovan@wusa9.com, tkopania@wusa9.com, sabrooks@wusa9.com, chernande1@wusa9.com

SUBJECT: EXPEDITED FOIA DEMAND: Vector Control Manifests, GPS Telemetry & Internal Communications (Lot 802 / Square 5812)

To the D.C. Health (DOH) FOIA Officer and Carl Filler:

Under the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq.), I am submitting an expedited demand for public records concerning the Department's emergency response to a documented biological and structural hazard located at the artificial retention basin on Lot 802, Square 5812 (adjacent to 1488-1500 Morris Rd SE).

On Saturday, September 12, 2026, I filed an urgent code-enforcement complaint with D.C. Health demanding immediate vector abatement (larviciding) and emergency fencing for this toxic, stagnant overflow pond. On Monday, September 14, 2026, at 10:00 AM, DOH Chief of Staff Carl Filler confirmed in writing that a D.C. Health vector control team had visited the site and treated the pond with a long-acting larvicide. Mr. Filler, however, failed to address the simultaneous demand for emergency safety fencing to mitigate the attractive nuisance and drowning hazard under D.C. Code § 6-801.
To ensure total transparency regarding the Department's official recognition and remediation of this site, I am formally requesting copies of the following records generated between Saturday, September 12, 2026, and the date this request is processed:

1. Certified Work Orders & Chemical Manifests: The official D.C. Health field inspection report, technician work order, and the specific EPA registration number/manifest for the 6-month larvicide deployed at Lot 802, Square 5812, on or prior to September 14, 2026.
2. GPS/AVL Vehicle Telemetry: All GPS coordinates, Automatic Vehicle Location (AVL) data, and dispatch logs for the specific D.C. Health or District Vector Control vehicle that visited the 1400-1500 blocks of Morris Rd SE to conduct this treatment.
3. Internal Communications & Frantic Forwarding (Carl Filler): Digital telemetry confirms that my September 12 emergency demand was opened and/or forwarded internally over 40 times on the morning of September 14, just prior to Mr. Filler's response. I demand all emails, internal memorandums, Microsoft Teams chat transcripts, and forwarded messages sent from, received by, or CC'd to Carl Filler regarding Lot 802, Morris Rd SE, vector abatement, or Fred Gamble during this timeframe.4. Interagency Coordination & Fencing Refusal: Any communications between Carl Filler, Director Ayanna Bennett, or D.C. Health staff and representatives from the Department of Energy & Environment (DOEE), Department of Buildings (DOB), or District Department of Transportation (DDOT) regarding the jurisdictional responsibility of the pond, or the justification for refusing to mandate emergency safety fencing around the hazard.

Format of Production Demand:
All electronic records, emails, and telemetry data must be produced in their native, rich metadata format. Scrubbed, flattened, or digitally altered files will not be accepted. 

Fee Waiver Request:
I request a waiver of all fees associated with this request pursuant to D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b). Disclosure of this information is strictly in the public interest. The records will expose how D.C. Health triages imminent biological hazards threatening residential properties in Ward 8. Because the WUSA-9 investigative team is actively monitoring this municipal infrastructure failure, the disclosed information will be broadly disseminated to ensure strict government accountability. 

If my request is denied in whole or part, I require a detailed justification citing specific statutory exemptions for every redaction.  
Attachments: 
https://youtube.com/shorts/J4MsQ-rKfmE?si=5XlOIEyYT2kPf3_S
https://youtube.com/shorts/J4MsQ-rKfmE?si=IXJuMEj5X8mAOWl4

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: CBP secondary statistics
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Periodic (monthly or quarterly) statistical reports, summaries, or dashboards that CBP field offices and/or individual ports of entry submit to CBP Headquarters and/or DHS leadership regarding referrals to secondary inspection. This includes any recurring management reports, situational awareness reports, or "signif" reports used to track secondary inspection volume, whether produced automatically by border-management software (e.g., TECS, ATS, or successor systems) or compiled manually by field office staff.

Specifically, I am requesting that these records, to the extent they exist in this form, include or be broken out by:

- The number or rate of travelers referred to secondary inspection at each individual port of entry (land, air, and sea), by month or quarter;
- A breakdown by citizenship/immigration status — specifically distinguishing U.S. citizens from non-U.S. citizens (including lawful permanent residents, visa holders, and undocumented individuals) — where such a breakdown is captured in the reporting;
- Any accompanying narrative, footnotes, or explanatory memoranda field offices attach when transmitting these figures to headquarters.

Time period: September 2022 through September 2026

Format: I request records be provided electronically in their native, non-image format (e.g., Excel, CSV, or searchable PDF) where feasible, since some responsive records may originate as spreadsheets or database exports.

Note on scope: I am requesting the aggregate/statistical reports described above — not individual travelers' case files, personally identifiable information, or law-enforcement records tied to specific encounters. If any portion of a responsive report contains personally identifying details, I request that CBP redact those details and release the remainder rather than withholding the full record.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

title: Frances Stonor Saunders (historian of CIA and culture)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Frances Stonor Saunders (historian of CIA and culture)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records mentioning, relating to, or generated as a result of investigation or inquiry into historian Frances Hélène Jeanne Stonor Saunders FRSL (14 April 1966 – 31 August 2026), or her book, "Who Paid the Piper?: CIA and the Cultural Cold War." Her death is widely-known and widely reported; as such, privacy concerns under FOIA Exemptions 6 and 7 are voided, as are any concerns under the Privacy Act. For example, you may find her obituary from The Guardian at the following link: https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/sep/13/frances-stonor-saunders-obiituary

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records of both HQ and all field offices for all relevant names, agencies, organizations, companies and events including but not limited to those cited in the previous paragraphs and/or links as well as a cross-reference with the Southern Poverty Law Center to include any information provided by the SPLC. My request includes but is not limited to 137, 157, 176, 177, 183, 184, 188, and 214 files. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

If any part of these documents are exempt from disclosure, please be sure to review and release all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions of responsive documents, as the FOIA requires.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

Upload documents directly: https://www.muckrock.com/respond/2397184/" After reviewing your request, it has been determined that responsive records exist. Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(b)(1)(A) you are hereby notified that due to the extensive nature of your request Gwinnett County cannot provide these documents within three (3) business days. 
In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(b)(1), you are hereby notified that the documents include all records requested we have pertaining to HIDTA funding from 1/1/2022-9/14/2026.  Additionally, the County has documents or portions of documents that may be responsive to your requests which are exempt from disclosure pursuant to the following, 
O.C.G.A. § 50-18-72(a)(20)-Records that reveal an individual's personal information that is exempt from disclosure. 
O.C.G.A. § 50-18-72(a)(43)-Records containing tax matters or tax information that is confidential under state or federal law. 
Gwinnett County is authorized by law to charge reasonable search, retrieval, and production costs to fulfill your request.  As provided by O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(c)(1), you are notified that the estimated cost to search, retrieve, redact, copy, produce and/or supervise inspection of the requested documents is .  This is calculated as follows:  a charge of $31.89 per hour for 34 hours after the first fifteen minutes. $1,076.29 Further pursuant to O.C.G.A. §50-18-71(d), Gwinnett County is authorized to require prepayment of estimate costs prior to production of records where the estimated cost to produce exceeds $500.00. Therefore, as the cost to search, retrieve, redact, and copy the documents responsive to your request exceeds $500.00, Gwinnett County is requesting that you pay the search and retrieval costs of $1,076.29 prior to Gwinnett County beginning production of this request.  Once we receive your prepayment, staff will begin the search and retrieval process and estimates that the documents and final costs will be ready within 25 business days from the date we receive your prepayment. 
Sincerely, 
Cassidy Elliott
